attribution.note: Marcus directly asserts the comparison in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the study-specific comparison and no-persona condition. Surrounding text reasonably identifies the relevant model as GPT-4.5.

contract.note: Using GPT-4.5 follows the surrounding discussion. Comparing reported overall win rates is an ordinary reading of the unqualified comparison; Marcus specifies neither a population nor statistical significance.

evidence.note: The original preprint predates the statement and reports GPT-4.5 without a persona at 36%, versus ELIZA at 23%. GPT-4o's 21% concerns a different model. Lack of statistical significance does not establish that ELIZA had the higher reported rate.

reviews.rationale: Under the fair contextual identification of ChatGPT as GPT-4.5, the paper reports a higher overall win rate for the no-persona model than for ELIZA. The lower GPT-4o result and the significance qualification do not support the specified GPT-4.5 comparison.
